solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Light blue line on clean cake

parts.note: the Victoria line is shown in light blue on the London Underground map
to sponge something is to wipe it clean

explanation.surface: Someone tidies up a pale blue line on a cake while icing it.
explanation.walkthrough: The London Underground colours each line; the Victoria line is the light blue one.
explanation.definitionFit: A Victoria sponge is a classic British layered sponge filled with jam and cream, a specific kind of cake.

clue.text: Barking hounds bay?

indicators.note: barking is slang for mad, and mad letters are scrambled out of their order

explanation.surface: Hunting dogs bark and bay, as hounds do.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bay' looks like the noise hounds make, but it is the definition: a named bay in Canada. The question mark flags the example.
explanation.definitionFit: Hudson Bay is the vast inland sea in northern Canada, so the name is one example of a bay.

clue.text: Uninteresting building is remote

indicators.note: building means constructing something new, so the following letters are assembled into a fresh order

explanation.surface: A dull building stands far from anywhere.
explanation.definitionFit: Something tiresome bores and wearies people, so it is dull and lacks any interest.

clue.text: Very reasonable, when off to choir practice?

definitions.meaning: first meaning: sold cheaply, a bargain
second meaning, taken literally: setting out to fetch some music to sing

explanation.surface: A singer heads off to choir practice, and the price is right.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark marks the literal, whimsical reading of an everyday idiom.
explanation.definitionFit: Something going for a song is being sold for very little money, a phrase meaning cheap or a bargain.

clue.text: All the bombs — are so?

indicators.note: bombs blow things apart, so the preceding letters are blasted into another order

explanation.surface: A question: is every bomb deadly?
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue is both the wordplay and the definition: blow up two words and you get what bombs are.
explanation.definitionFit: Bombs are designed to kill, so all of them can be described as deadly, capable of causing death.

clue.text: Ruby celebrated throwing male attire into river

indicators.note: throwing one thing into another places it inside, together with the word into that follows
into says the attire ends up inside the river

parts.note: the Forth is a Scottish river
a tie is worn by men

explanation.surface: At a ruby wedding party someone throws a man's tie into a river.
explanation.walkthrough: A ruby wedding anniversary marks forty years, so 'Ruby celebrated' is the anniversary being celebrated.
explanation.definitionFit: Ruby is the traditional gift for a fortieth wedding anniversary, so that is the anniversary celebrated with rubies.

clue.text: One sister and one boy together

parts.note: a nun is a religious sister

explanation.surface: A sister and a boy are seen together.
explanation.definitionFit: Doing things in unison means acting simultaneously and in agreement, which is acting jointly.

clue.text: Winter's ending, nothing stopping return of insects — spring back!

indicators.note: ending asks for only the final letter of the word before it
a return goes back the way it came, so the word is read backwards
stopping here means plugging a gap, so it sits inside the other word

parts.note: zero, shaped like the letter O

explanation.surface: As winter ends, insects return, and the reader is told to leap back.
explanation.definitionFit: To recoil is to jump or flinch backwards, as a gun does when fired or a person in shock.

clue.text: New tiled roof with shelf for book

indicators.note: a new version is a remade one, so the letters that follow come out in a different order

explanation.surface: A builder fits a freshly tiled roof plus a shelf to hold a book.
explanation.definitionFit: Lord of the Flies is William Golding's novel about stranded schoolboys, an example of a book.

clue.text: Husband into creation of a rapper, best artist

indicators.note: into says the husband goes inside the rearranged letters
a creation is something made up, so these letters are fashioned into a new order

explanation.surface: A husband gets into making a rapper the best artist.
explanation.definitionFit: The Pre-Raphaelite Brotherhood was a group of Victorian painters, so a member is a type of artist.

clue.text: Sample last of paintings framed by patron of the arts

indicators.note: a frame surrounds a picture, so one piece sits within the other

parts.note: Henry Tate, the sugar magnate whose collection founded London's Tate gallery

indicators.note: last of takes only the final letter of the following word

explanation.surface: An art patron's framed paintings are being sampled.
explanation.walkthrough: Henry Tate was a Victorian sugar merchant who gave his art collection to found the Tate gallery in London.
explanation.definitionFit: To taste something is to try a small amount of it, which is the verb sample.

clue.text: Brilliant guide, Jack goes past prickly thorns

indicators.note: going past means coming after, so the sailor follows the other piece
prickly suggests something bristling and out of shape, so the letters are reworked

parts.note: jack and tar are both old words for a sailor

explanation.surface: A brilliant guide called Jack leads walkers past thorny bushes.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Brilliant' reads as praise for a person, but it means shining brightly.
explanation.definitionFit: Polaris, the pole star, shines brightly and has long been used by navigators to find north.

clue.text: Stop talking, as prepared for divorce?

definitions.meaning: first meaning: end a telephone call
second meaning, taken literally: with the wedding band removed

explanation.surface: A spouse stops speaking, ready to end the marriage.
explanation.walkthrough: To ring off is the British phrase for hanging up the phone; read literally, it describes a wedding band taken off.
explanation.definitionFit: Ringing off ends a phone conversation, and a removed wedding band signals the marriage is over.

clue.text: Overlie grotesque, outstanding art?

indicators.note: grotesque means distorted and misshapen, so the word before it is twisted out of shape

explanation.surface: A grotesque decoration lies over an outstanding work of art.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Outstanding' reads as excellent, but here it means standing out from a surface.
explanation.definitionFit: Relievo is sculpture in relief, where figures project from a flat background, so the art literally stands out.

clue.text: When Panama falls quickly?

definitions.meaning: first meaning, taken literally: the moment a Panama, a straw hat, is let fall

explanation.surface: It sounds like the fall of a Central American country happening fast.
explanation.walkthrough: Panama looks like the country, but it is a lightweight straw hat; the question mark flags the literal reading of the idiom.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom describes acting at once, from the old practice of dropping a hat as a starting signal.

clue.text: Make taco for Judas?

parts.note: surface reading: an order to cook a Mexican snack
setter's reading: the instruction that rearranges the letters of an overcoat into a taco, which names a traitor

explanation.surface: Someone is asked to cook a taco for Judas.
explanation.walkthrough: Read the answer as two words: an instruction to rearrange the letters of a garment, which turns them into taco.
explanation.definitionFit: Judas betrayed Jesus, so his name stands for a traitor, someone who switches to the other side.

clue.text: Effervescent pond life absorbing light

indicators.note: absorbing means taking something in, so one piece is held inside the other

parts.note: a frog is a creature of ponds
light, as of fabric, means thin

explanation.surface: Bubbling pond life soaks up the sunlight.
explanation.definitionFit: Effervescent liquid fizzes with bubbles, and foaming or frothing describes that bubbling surface.

clue.text: Criminals good with taxes

parts.note: PI, short for pious, is crossword shorthand for good
rates are local property taxes in Britain

explanation.surface: Criminals are portrayed as good at handling taxes.
explanation.walkthrough: Rates are the British local taxes on property.
explanation.definitionFit: Pirates rob ships at sea or copy goods illegally, so they are lawbreakers.

clue.text: Obvious fact is concealed by inadequate US president

indicators.note: concealed by says one word is hidden within the other
inadequate means falling short, so the name loses its final letter

explanation.surface: An inadequate US president hides an obvious fact.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Inadequate' looks like a political jibe, but it says the surname falls one letter short.
explanation.definitionFit: A truism is a statement so self-evident that it hardly needs saying, a plain truth.

clue.text: Job held by bitter missionary

indicators.note: something held by another is gripped inside it

parts.note: bitter is a British style of beer, an ale

explanation.surface: A sour missionary holds down a job.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bitter' reads as resentful, but it is the British pale beer.
explanation.definitionFit: The apostles were sent out by Jesus to spread his teaching, and the word now means any pioneering missionary.

clue.text: Artist, giant touring Italy

indicators.note: touring means going round, so one piece wraps around the other

parts.note: I is the international vehicle code for Italy

explanation.surface: A giant of an artist goes on tour around Italy.
explanation.definitionFit: Titian was the great Venetian Renaissance painter, so he is an example of an artist.

clue.text: Acorn and nut lost, left in the dark

indicators.note: lost suggests wandering astray, so the letters lose their original order

explanation.surface: A squirrel has lost an acorn and a nut and is left in the dark.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Left' reads as abandoned, but it is the letter L.
explanation.definitionFit: Nocturnal describes what happens or is active at night, when it is dark.

clue.text: Holiday accommodation — India next?

definitions.meaning: first meaning: a place to stay while away
second meaning: in the NATO phonetic alphabet, the code word just before India

explanation.surface: A traveller books a room and wonders whether India is the next stop.
explanation.walkthrough: In the radio alphabet H and I are spoken as two words in sequence, so the H word is followed by India.
explanation.definitionFit: A hotel lodges travellers, and it is the radio code word for H, which India comes after.

clue.text: Pass first of exams before blunder

indicators.note: before says that piece comes ahead of the next in the line
first of takes only the opening letter of the following word

parts.note: a lapse is a slip or blunder

explanation.surface: A student passes the first exam before making a blunder.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Pass' reads as succeeding in an exam, but it is the verb used of time going by.
explanation.definitionFit: Time is said to elapse or pass as it goes by, so the two verbs are synonyms.

clue.text: Very old guru breathing in air

indicators.note: breathing in takes something inside the body, so one piece goes within the other

parts.note: a sage is a wise teacher or guru
an air is a tune, and tone is a musical sound

explanation.surface: An ancient guru breathes deeply.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Air' looks like what is breathed, but it means a melody.
explanation.definitionFit: The Stone Age is the prehistoric era, so the phrase is used informally for anything extremely old-fashioned.
